posts.title: Heat, desiccation and restrained props: climate volatility is a temporary works load
posts.excerpt: Ground Engineering published on 9 October 2026 an industry view by Vicky Mastoridou CEng MICE of Groundforce Shorco examining thermal loading and soil volatility in temporary works. Sustained temperatures above 30°C, desiccation cracking in clays and subsequent intense rainfall can change the ground parameters assumed at the design stage. Exposed hydraulic props, sheet piles and bracing frames absorb solar radiation; because they are restrained they convert thermal expansion into additional axial compression that consumes capacity calculated under BS EN 1997. Designers may be forced to specify denser or stronger propping, reducing working clearance. Winter or spring ground investigation is no longer a reliable basis for a heatwave construction phase.

Heat and desiccation are temporary works loads. A winter ground investigation does not automatically remain valid through a 30°C+ construction summer.

On 9 October 2026 Ground Engineering published an industry view by Vicky Mastoridou CEng MICE, development manager at Groundforce Shorco. Sustained thermal loads above 30°C, widespread desiccation and shifting water tables can no longer be treated as short-term anomalies. In clay-rich soils, extended dry spells shrink and crack the ground, altering stiffness and strength. Subsequent rainfall then penetrates those cracks rapidly, causing localised softening, swelling and sudden spikes in lateral earth pressure.

The same heat acts on the temporary works themselves. Exposed hydraulic props, sheet piles and bracing frames absorb solar radiation. Because they are fully restrained between walls, walers and slabs they cannot expand freely. The restraint converts thermal energy into additional compressive axial force. That force consumes part of the resistance calculated under BS EN 1997 partial factors. The prop that was sized for earth pressure alone may now be carrying a significant thermal component. To stay within capacity the designer may need stronger or denser propping, which reduces working clearance inside the excavation.

Put thermal range, solar gain and the possibility of changing ground parameters into the design brief and the inspection regime. Monitoring that cannot distinguish a thermal spike from genuine ground movement is incomplete. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A proprietary hydraulic prop with a published capacity is not low risk if the thermal allowance was based on historic averages that the site has already exceeded.

body.p: On 9 October 2026 Ground Engineering published an industry-view article by Vicky Mastoridou CEng MICE, development manager at Groundforce Shorco, titled Redefining geotechnical limits: thermal loading and soil volatility in temporary works. The piece argues that record-breaking heatwaves and the summer of 2026 have exposed a design vulnerability: temporary works and shoring schemes are increasingly required to operate beyond the climatic envelopes assumed at design. Sustained temperatures above 30°C, widespread desiccation and shifting water tables can no longer be treated as short-term weather anomalies. In clay-rich formations such as London Clay, extended dry spells cause shrinkage and cracking that change stiffness and strength. Subsequent intense rainfall then penetrates those cracks rapidly, producing localised softening, swelling and pore-water conditions that can spike lateral earth pressures faster than conventional models anticipate. At the same time, exposed structural steelwork — hydraulic props, sheet piles and bracing frames — absorbs direct solar radiation, driving surface temperatures above ambient. Because these members are restrained between retaining walls, walers and slabs they cannot expand freely; the restraint converts thermal energy into additional compressive axial force. That force consumes part of the structural resistance calculated under BS EN 1997 partial factors. To remain within capacity, designers may need to specify stronger or denser propping layouts, which reduces internal working clearance. The article concludes that the critical question is no longer whether a heatwave is likely, but how the temporary works will perform under the extreme event, and that ground assessment, thermal modelling and real-time monitoring should be embedded from the start.

Excavation support, propping and temporary retaining structures are temporary works. Their performance depends on both the ground parameters assumed in the design brief and the loads the support system itself must carry. CDM 2015 requires construction work to be planned, managed and monitored. BS 5975-1:2024 is the code of practice for a temporary works procedure; it is not a statute and it does not appoint a person. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy. BS EN 1997-1 and its UK National Annex govern geotechnical design; the partial factors and load combinations used for temporary states should be those appropriate to the temporary works design, not simply copied from a permanent-works calculation. A ground investigation carried out in winter or spring does not automatically remain valid through a prolonged heatwave and subsequent rainfall. Desiccation cracking followed by rapid infiltration can change undrained strength, stiffness and pore pressures within the life of the temporary works. Thermal expansion in restrained props is an additional load case, not a secondary effect that can be ignored because the prop has a manufacturer’s capacity. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A proprietary hydraulic prop whose capacity is stated at a reference temperature is not low risk if the site has already recorded surface temperatures that generate axial forces consuming a substantial fraction of that capacity. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: State the expected temperature range, solar-gain exposure and the possibility of changing ground parameters (desiccation, subsequent rainfall, groundwater fluctuation) in the design brief for any propping or excavation-support scheme.
Require the temporary works designer to identify the thermal load component separately from the geotechnical load and to show the residual capacity available for earth pressure.
Do not treat a winter or spring ground investigation as sufficient for a summer construction phase without a review of whether desiccation or rainfall has altered the parameters used in the design.
Where load cells or monitoring are installed, ensure the interpretation method can distinguish a thermal spike from genuine ground movement. An alert that cannot be attributed is not a control.
If denser or stronger propping is required to accommodate thermal loads, confirm that the reduced working clearance is still compatible with the plant, access and sequence in the method statement.

Inspect and re-assess after any prolonged heat or heavy rainfall that could affect either the ground or the restrained steelwork. Record the inspection. A daily visual check that does not consider temperature is incomplete.
Do not proceed until the arrangement has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Based on the Ground Engineering industry-view article of 9 October 2026. It is not a design, a check or a statement that any particular propping arrangement is adequate or inadequate under thermal loading. No soil parameters, temperature ranges, prop capacities or axial forces have been calculated here. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.

posts.title: Unsupported trench, spoil at the edge: the Banstead collapse was temporary works, not a surprise
posts.excerpt: On 9 September 2026 the Old Bailey sentenced Appledorn Developments Limited and T Vaughan Limited after Gheorghita Arsene, 33, was killed when an unsupported trench collapsed at Park Road, Banstead, Surrey on 24 June 2020. He was buried under approximately two tonnes of soil while working at the bottom of a deep excavation dug with a three-tonne digger to replace a damaged pipe. The joint Surrey Police and HSE investigation found no supports in the trench and excavated soil deposited immediately next to the edge. Earlier the same day a self-employed contracts manager had observed another worker in the same unsupported excavation and failed to ensure measures were in place. T Vaughan Limited was fined £650,000; Appledorn Developments Limited £500,000. The contracts manager received a suspended sentence. An unsupported excavation with a surcharge at the crest is temporary works. It is not a routine dig.
posts.linkedinReady:
An unsupported trench with spoil piled at the edge is temporary works. The Banstead sentencing shows what happens when that fact is treated as optional.

On 9 September 2026 the Old Bailey sentenced principal contractor Appledorn Developments Limited and subcontractor T Vaughan Limited after Gheorghita Arsene, 33, was killed on 24 June 2020 when the walls of a deep trench collapsed at Park Road, Banstead. He was clearing soil at the bottom of an excavation dug with a three-tonne digger to replace a damaged pipe. He was buried under approximately two tonnes of soil.

The joint investigation found no supports in the trench and excavated soil deposited immediately next to the edge. Earlier the same day a self-employed contracts manager working for T Vaughan Limited had observed another worker in the same unsupported excavation. He knew measures were required. He did not ensure they were in place. T Vaughan Limited was fined £650,000. Appledorn Developments Limited was fined £500,000. The contracts manager received a 10-month sentence, suspended for 18 months.

CDM 2015 requires excavations to be planned and managed so that they do not collapse. Spoil next to the crest is a surcharge. An unsupported face is a temporary works item. A contracts manager who sees the condition and walks past it is not a substitute for a design brief, a support system, a permit and an inspection. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A shallow dig can become high consequence the moment a person is inside it.

Put every excavation that a person will enter on the temporary works register. Do not treat the absence of a trench box as a saving.

body.p: On 9 September 2026, following a trial at the Old Bailey, principal contractor Appledorn Developments Limited and subcontractor T Vaughan Limited were convicted of breaching Section 3(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. Gheorghita Arsene, 33, died on 24 June 2020 at a site on Park Road, Banstead, Surrey when the walls of a deep trench collapsed while he was working at the bottom to replace a damaged pipe. The trench had been dug with a three-tonne digger. He was clearing soil with a shovel and a pickaxe when the sides failed. He was buried under approximately two tonnes of soil and died at the scene. A joint investigation by Surrey Police and the Health and Safety Executive found there were no supports in the trench and that excavated soil had been deposited immediately next to the edge. Earlier the same day Anthony O’Connor, a self-employed contracts manager working for T Vaughan Limited, had observed another worker in the same unsupported excavation. As an experienced contracts manager he knew suitable measures were required to prevent a collapse but failed to ensure they were implemented. T Vaughan Limited was fined £650,000 and ordered to pay costs of £40,000. Appledorn Developments Limited was fined £500,000. O’Connor pleaded guilty on 22 May 2026 to breaching Section 7 of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and was sentenced to 10 months’ imprisonment, suspended for 18 months, with 150 hours of unpaid work. The prosecution was brought by the Crown Prosecution Service. HSE does not set the fine.

An excavation that a person will enter, or that can affect persons or adjacent assets if it fails, is temporary works. CDM 2015 requires the principal contractor to plan, manage and monitor the construction phase, and requires contractors to plan, manage and monitor their own work. Regulation 22 of CDM 2015 specifically addresses excavations and requires suitable and sufficient steps to prevent them from collapsing or causing a person to be buried or trapped. Spoil deposited next to the crest is a surcharge load. The absence of support is not a neutral condition; it is an unsupported temporary face. BS 5975-1:2024 is the code of practice for a temporary works procedure. It is not a statute and it does not appoint a person. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy. The temporary works procedure should identify the excavation, require a design brief where the geometry, ground, surcharge or sequence makes a standard solution inadequate, and control the permit-to-enter and the inspection regime. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A short trench for a pipe replacement becomes high consequence the moment a person is working at the bottom with an unsupported face and a spoil heap at the edge. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Enter every excavation that a person will enter, or that can affect adjacent structures, services or the public, on the temporary works register. A digger ticket is not a register entry.

Confirm the design brief states depth, length, ground conditions, groundwater, existing services, adjacent structures and the surcharge from plant and spoil. Spoil must not be deposited next to the crest unless the design specifically allows it.

Do not allow entry until a suitable support system (trench box, sheets and frames, or other designed arrangement) is in place and the permit-to-enter has been issued. An unsupported face is not a temporary works solution.
The contracts manager who sees an unsupported excavation and walks past it is not the control. The control is the procedure that stops the work until the support is installed.

Inspect the support before each shift and after any event that could affect stability (heavy rain, plant movement, ground heave). Record the inspection. A daily visual glance without competence or authority is not an inspection.
If the sequence requires the support to be removed or altered to complete the pipe work, that change is a temporary works alteration. It requires review before it is made.
Do not proceed until the arrangement has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

It is not a design, a check or a statement that any particular support system would have been adequate or inadequate on the day. No ground parameters, depths or loads have been calculated here. posts.title: A protection deck over a live bridge is temporary works — the Tyne Bridge closure is the control, not the design
posts.excerpt: Newcastle City Council confirmed on 8 October 2026 that the Tyne Bridge will close from 11pm on Friday 23 October until 5am on Monday 2 November so scaffolders can install an overhead protection deck ahead of main-arch restoration in early 2027. Independent scaffold legs will run along both footpaths. Twin aluminium beams will span between them. Scaffold boards and temporary carriageway lighting complete the deck. Esh Construction is the contractor. The full closure is the measure that makes erection over the carriageway possible. A protection deck that keeps a public crossing open under grit-blasting and steelwork repair is temporary works, not a traffic arrangement.
posts.linkedinReady:
A protection deck over a live bridge is temporary works. The 10-day closure is the control that makes the erection possible, not a substitute for the design.

On 8 October 2026 Newcastle City Council confirmed the Tyne Bridge will close from 11pm on Friday 23 October until 5am on Monday 2 November. Independent scaffold legs will be installed along both footpaths, with a new arrangement on the east side to mirror the west. Twin aluminium beams will span between the footpaths to form the main structure. Scaffold boards and temporary carriageway lighting complete the deck — a working platform above and protection for the public below.

Esh Construction’s construction manager said the work above the carriageway cannot be undertaken safely while the bridge remains open. Up to 70% of the deck is planned during the full closure. The rest follows in weekday overnight vehicle closures in November. A 4.95 m height restriction will apply once the deck is in place.

The legs, the beams, the boards, the lighting and the sequence are temporary works. The load path runs from the deck into the aluminium beams, into the independent legs on the footpaths, and into whatever those legs bear on. Existing parapet scaffold, wind, grit-blasting later, and the public underneath are all interfaces. A closure that is not in the temporary works procedure is only a traffic order.

Put the protection deck on the register. Do not treat the half-term window as the design.

body.p: On 8 October 2026 Newcastle City Council published an update confirming that the Tyne Bridge will close completely from 11pm on Friday 23 October until 5am on Monday 2 November 2026. The closure allows advanced scaffolders to work around the clock installing a protection deck above the carriageway ahead of main steel-arch restoration planned for early 2027. Independent scaffold legs will be installed along the east and west footpaths, including a new arrangement on the east side to mirror the existing west-side scaffold. Twin aluminium beams will span between the footpaths to form the main structure of the protection deck. Scaffold boards and temporary carriageway lighting will complete the installation, creating a working platform and providing protection for the works above and the public below. Up to 70 per cent of the deck is expected to be completed during the full closure. The remainder will be installed during weekday overnight vehicle closures lasting up to four weeks in November, with pedestrian and cycle access retained during those overnight periods. A 4.95 m vehicle height restriction will be introduced once the deck is in place; double-decker buses are not affected. Esh Construction is delivering the restoration for Newcastle City Council and Gateshead Council. Stephen McClean, construction manager at Esh Construction, stated that the construction of the protection deck requires extensive work above the carriageway which cannot be undertaken safely while the bridge remains open to vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists. The councils note that the programme remains on schedule to finish ahead of the bridge’s centenary in October 2028. Scaffmag reported the same arrangements on 8 October 2026.

A protection deck spanning a live public highway, carried on independent scaffold legs and aluminium beams, is temporary works. It is not a traffic-management detail and it is not a temporary fence. The deck must carry its own self-weight, temporary construction loads, wind, and later the grit-blasting and steelwork repair operations above it, while protecting the public below. CDM 2015 requires construction work to be planned, managed and monitored. The Work at Height Regulations 2005 require work at height to be properly planned, appropriately supervised and carried out so far as is reasonably practicable safely. BS 5975-1:2024 is the code of practice for a temporary works procedure. It is not a statute and it does not appoint a person. Exact clause references should be confirmed against the project’s licensed copy. TG20:21 and the scaffold designer’s calculations are manufacturer and industry requirements where they form part of the design. The independent legs, the twin aluminium beams, the board deck, the temporary lighting, the interface with the existing west-side parapet scaffold, and the sequence of erection under a full closure are all items that belong on the temporary works register. A 10-day half-term closure is a control measure that removes public interface during the highest-risk erection phase. It is not itself the design. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A proprietary aluminium beam with a published capacity is not low risk if the legs have no verified bearing, if the sequence leaves an incomplete span over the carriageway, or if the later height restriction is treated as a traffic sign rather than a temporary-works constraint. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Enter the protection deck, the independent legs, the aluminium beams and the temporary lighting on the temporary works register. A bridge closure order is not a register entry.
Confirm the design brief states the loads the deck must carry now and later — self-weight, temporary works loads, wind, grit-blasting plant and the public-protection requirement underneath.
Verify the bearing and fixings of the independent scaffold legs on both footpaths. Existing parapet scaffold on the west side is an interface, not a free support.
Treat the twin aluminium beams as a designed span. Do not complete the deck by placing boards across an uncalculated gap.

The full closure is the control that removes pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles during the main erection. The method statement must show that the incomplete structure is stable at every stage, including overnight.
The remaining 30% installed under overnight vehicle closures still needs a permit and an inspection regime. Pedestrian access during those nights is a public interface.
The 4.95 m height restriction is a temporary works consequence. Signage and enforcement are traffic measures; the restriction itself comes from the deck.
Do not proceed until the arrangement has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

It is not a design, a scaffold check or a statement that the published arrangement is adequate or inadequate. No loads, capacities or foundation values have been calculated here. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.
